Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players make their way out to the middle. Sharmin Akhter and Shamima Sultana are the openers for Bangladesh Women. Katherine Brunt to start with the ball. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then! 235 is what Bangladesh Women have in front of them. The nature of the pitch is slow and that will make life hard for Bangladesh batters. They have had their struggles in this tournament but if they get going in this match, we are in for a treat. Stay tuned to see how the chase unfolds.

Amy Jones is in for a chat. She says the wicket felt a little tricky. Adds that Bangladesh bowled really well and made it difficult to score runs at a good rate. Mentions, they can learn from the opposition of how they kept them under control and says she is happy with the score on the board.

Just like against Australia, Bangladesh Women are also playing their first-ever ODI against England Women but it never looked like it. The bowlers were very impressive right from the start and tightened the screws with two early wickets. They continued to maintain the pressure and made sure the runs were hard to come by. They got timely wickets but leaked a little more than they would have liked at the death. It's a still good performance from them and it is upto their batters now to spoil the party for England.

England Women didn't have the best of starts as they lost two early wickets. That put them under pressure but Tammy Beaumont and Natalie Sciver weathered the storm by building a slow but steady partnership. However, Beaumont never got going and fell ultimately and Sciver also followed her soon. It was Sophia Dunkley and Amy Jones then who did the rebuilding work and resurrected their side out of danger. Every batter struggled but Dunkley looked very comfortable and played a fine knock which has helped England put up a good total on the board.

Bangladesh kept control for the most part but those 43 runs in the last 5 overs would hurt them. Dunkley has played a sensational knock for England and they would feel they have got enough on the board. They would fancy their chances here and seal the semi final spot with a win.

Fahima Khatun later does enough to convince her skipper. Nigar Sultana takes the review. The UltraEdge shows no bat is involved. The Ball Tracking shows three reds and Natalie Sciver's time at the crease comes to an end. Sophia Dunkley is the new batter in.

Bangladesh Women have taken a review for LBW. UltraEdge shows a flat line as the ball passes the bat. Ball Tracking shows that the impact is outside off, it is pitching in line and wickets hitting. Excellent review from Bangladesh Women and the on-field decision will be overturned.

Natalie Sciver is the new batter in.

It is touch short, wide outside off. Heather Knight tries to play away from her body. She might've gotten thinnest of outside edge on it, as Nigar Sultana puts in a loud appeal from behind the stumps. Although the umpire is unmoved. Nigar Sultana is quite certain she heard something and takes the review instantly. The UltraEdge shows a spike as the ball passes the blade. Heather Knight has to walk back on a timid score.
Commentary.Howout: c Nigar Sultana b Salma Khatun

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller, on off. Heather Knight sweeps it to deep square leg for a couple.
Length, on off. Tammy Beaumont blocks it out watchfully. Bangladesh Women have done really well to tighten the screws after picking up the wicket.
Short ball, outside off. Heather Knight punches it to point for a single.
WIDE! On a length, wide outside off. Heather Knight leaves it alone. Wide called.
Full length, outside off. Heather Knight drives it through point for a couple now.
Full length, on the stumps. Heather Knight presses forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Good length, outside off. Heather Knight taps it to point.
Length ball, on off, blocked out solidly.

Slower through the air, full and on off. Tammy Beaumont tries to reverse sweep it but could not get enough power on her shot. Just two runs off the over. Bangladesh Women have been very impressive up front.
On off, blocked back to the bowler.
Short ball, outside off. Tammy Beaumont punches it to cover.
Looped up, on middle and leg. Tammy Beaumont defends it to mid-wicket.
Floated, full and on the stumps. Tammy Beaumont gets low and paddles it to fine leg for a brace.
Full and outside off. Tammy Beaumont defends it to cover on the front foot.
Full and outside off. Pushed to cover.
Length ball, outside off. Heather Knight works it to mid-wicket off the inner half.
Length ball, on leg. Tammy Beaumont looks to glance but misss. The ball goes off the pads to fine leg for a leg bye.
WIDE! Another ball down the leg side and it is given as wide.
Length ball, outside off. Tammy Beaumont chops it to the off side.
On a length, on leg. Heather Knight clips it to square leg for a single.

OUT! CAUGHT! Bangladesh Women get an early breakthrough! Jahanara Alam with a length ball, outside off. Danni Wyatt goes for the cut but cuts it uppishly and straight to point where Fahima Khatun takes a dolly. Bangladesh players are cock-a-hoop as they see the back of Danni Wyatt early.
Commentary.Howout: c Fahima Khatun b Jahanara Alam

Commentary.Commentary: Heather Knight comes in at number 3.
WIDE! Full and down leg, Danni Wyatt misses her flick. Wide called.
Full and on off, Tammy Beaumont again goes for the sweep but fails to connect it cleanly.
Flatter, outside off. Left alone.
Loopy ball, outside off, Tammy Beaumont looks to sweep but misses and the ball hits the grill of her helmet. A mandatory concussion test to follow.
Drops it short, on middle. Tammy Beaumont makes room and plays it late towards covers.
On the pads, Danni Wyatt turns it to square leg for a quick single.
Floats it up, on middle. Wyatt blocks it out.
Full and outside off, Tammy Beaumont drives it hard but straight to cover-point.
Full and attacking the stumps, Tammy Beaumont plays it to mid on.
Good-length ball, outside off. Tammy Beaumont lets it sail through.
On a length, outside off. Tammy Beaumont cracks it through covers. Doesn't have legs to go the fence but will get two runs.
Length, on off. Tammy Beaumont covers the line and defends it out.
Length ball, on middle. Tammy Beaumont looks to work it on the leg side but misses and gets hit on the thigh pad.
Outside off again, Danni Wyatt this time taps it to point.
FOUR! Cut away! Shortish, outside off. Danni Wyatt stays deep and cuts it past point for a boundary.
On the pads, Danni Wyatt works it to mid-wicket.
Loopy ball, outside off. Danni Wyatt pushes it towards covers.
Floats it up, on middle. Danni Wyatt shimmies down and blocks.
Loopy ball, on off. Danni Wyatt defends it out.
Salma Khatun to start with the new ball from the other end.

FOUR! Fuller in length, on off. Tammy Beaumont leans and crunches her drive towards extra cover. The fielder there misfields and the ball races away to the fence. Bangladesh Women need to be sharp in the field. They cannot afford to leak away such runs.
Danni Wyatt gets off the mark as well. Length ball, on leg. Wyatt clips it to mid-wicket for a run.
Good-length ball, on off. Danni Wyatt taps it to point.
WIDE! Full and going down the leg side, Danni Wyatt leaves it alone. Wided.
Good length, on off. Danni Wyatt taps it to point.
Tammy Beaumont and England Women are underway! Length ball, on middle. Tammy Beaumont turns it to mid-wicket for a single.
Jahanara Alam starts with a full ball, on off. Tammy Beaumont presses forward and defends it on the leg side.

Done with all the pre-match proceedings! Now, the Bangladesh players take the field. Followed by Tammy Beaumont and Danni Wyatt who walk out to open for England Women. But before the action begins, all the players unite to show their support for the BLM movement. Jahanara Alam to start with the new ball.
The game is set to begin. Both the teams stride out to the middle and get lined-up for their respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first, followed by the one of England.

PITCH REPORT - Nasser Hussain says Windy Wellington is living up to its name. Mentions that there is a breeze here but not strong. Tells that it's the same pitch that was used for Bangladesh Australia. Informs that the dimensions are same and slightly shorter on one side. Says that there is a little bit of grass on it but there are some rough patches on a very fullish length.

Nigar Sultana, the skipper of Bangladesh, is in for a chat. She says, they would’ve wanted to bat first as well. But believes her bowlers are enjoying a good run and hopes they can continue the good work. Mentions, they will try to hit the right areas with the ball and cause some problem to the England batters.

Heather Knight, the English skipper, says they are going to have a bat. Tells that it is the third game on this wicket but she still thinks it is going to be a good surface. Mentions that they want to score some runs and hopefully their spinners come in later on.

Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Sharmin Akhter, Shamima Sultana (In for Murshida Khatun), Fargana Hoque, Nigar Sultana (C/ WK), Rumana Ahmed, Ritu Moni, Lata Mondal, Salma Khatun, Fahima Khatun, Nahida Akter, Jahanara Alam.

England Women (Playing XI) - Tammy Beaumont, Danni Wyatt, Heather Knight (C), Natalie Sciver, Amy Jones (WK), Sophia Dunkley, Katherine Brunt, Sophie Ecclestone, Kate Cross, Charlotte Dean (In for Anya Shrubsole), Freya Davies (In for Emma Lamb).
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of England Women. They have opted to BAT first.

Bangladesh Women, on the other hand, are already out of the semi final contention and will look to spoil the party for England. They managed to win only 1 game in the entire tournament. They will be aiming to round off the competition with a win. England might be favourites but Bangladesh have given other teams a run for their money and have the potential for causing another upset. A cracking game beckons at Wellington. Toss and team news in a bit.

Defending champions England are in a good position at the moment but still have concerns over their qualification. They must win this match to make it to the semis. If they lose, then a lot will depend on other factors. They can't afford to lose this match and are firm favourites as well to win this encounter given the kind of form they are in.

This is the last day of the league fixtures before we head to the knockouts and in this penultimate match of the round robin, we will see England Women take on Bangladesh Women. Mind you that it's not a dead rubber as there are still two semi final spots up for grabs and a lot of that depends on this one. If England win, they seal their spot. As simple as that. Let's see if they are able to do that or not.
